title: Panels for Prevention: Margarita Muñiz Academy Student Presentation
description:
Lynn and Valerie have been working with the wonderful students at Margarita Muñiz Academy in Jamaica Plain as they prepare their project on gun violence prevention for the Aspen Challenge. Margarita Muñiz Academy competed against 16 other Boston area high schools a few weeks ago, and they were one of three schools chosen as the winners of this prestigious competition!

The students will be travelling to the Aspen Challenge the following week to present their winning project - but we get a sneak peek! Please join us on Thursday, June 17, at 11:30am to watch the video of the students' presentation. They will join us on the call for a Q&A session and to talk more about their project and their hopes for the future of gun violence prevention. 

This is a wonderful opportunity for mutual learning. We will get to hear directly from students whose lives have been drastically impacted by gun violence, and we will give them the opportunity to practice their presentation before they head to Aspen. We hope you can join us!

title: Mt. Sterling Ohio SB-1 Referendum Signature Collection
description:

Signatures also support getting this issues onto the ballot for voters to decide (vs. legislators who passed this bill w/o Ohio input). 

If implemented, Ohio Senate Bill 1 (SB 1) would radically alter how Ohio’s public colleges and universities are allowed to operate AND what they’re allowed to teach.
It would:
heavily restrict the teaching of “controversial” subjects such as climate change and current events
ban most diversity policies and programs
place departments, majors, and courses at risk
gut workers’ rights
ban meaningful tenure
ban academic partnerships with China
And much more
SB 1 is expected to be a major hit to Ohio’s economy. If it passes, Ohio would lose students, professors, tuition dollars, tourism dollars, and countless jobs. 

Let’s put SB-1 on the ballot!

title: Statewide Webinar: Supreme Court Review in U.S. v Skrmetti
description:
The U.S. Supreme Court should soon be issuing their decision in U.S. v Skrmetti, a key case involving individual states' efforts to ban essential, evidence-based, transgender health care for young people. 

In anticipation of this decision, we at Equality Michigan, along with our partners at the ACLU of Michigan, are offering this statewide virtual webinar to discuss the details and breadth of the decision, as well as how it does and does not impact Michiganders. 

The conversation will feature Emme Zanotti, Equality Michigan's Senior Director of Movement Building & Political Affairs; and Jay Kaplan, the ACLU of Michigan's LGBTQ+ Rights Project Staff Attorney.

There will be a Q&A portion of the webinar, where panelists can answer questions related both to the case, and to some other relevant issues impacting Michigan's LGBTQ+ community. 

In the event that a decision comes sooner in June, we may move this meeting up to more urgently answer your questions and try to address your concerns.

title: Pramila Jayapal's Resistance Lab Training 1.0 watch party with Activist Evenings
description:
The Resistance Lab is a series of trainings that are developed specifically for this moment. In this first lab, we look at how non-violent movements around the world have responded to leaders who seize power in authoritarian ways and the most effective tools and tactics to utilize in these moments. We offer frameworks to understand this moment at home, and incorporate interactive conversation with others to help create community and build our resistance movement.

The Resistance Lab was developed with experts who have researched and studied democratic backsliding around the world as well as in the United States and the non-violent movements that have emerged to challenge those authoritarian leaders. We also draw from many toolkits for effective tactics and frameworks as well as from Pramila’s own background leading successful organizing movements for economic and social justice for two decades.

Our goals are to help people understand how democracies fall and the most effective resistance movements that have challenged authoritarians and dictators; to turn anger, fear and frustration into action in the short-term while also preparing for a coordinated resistance movement for the longer term; and to build community across the country that can help grow our movement. At the end of the day, we want to get people strike-ready and street-ready and make sure we protect our people, our freedoms and our democracy.

With Trump and his MAGA billionaires doubling down on their attacks on the economic livelihoods of people to thrive and on our democracy, we can’t afford to sit this moment out. This is about building real power together. And it starts with you.

title: SPRINGFIELD Labor Day! Vote to Modernize Our Union!
description:
# Union Strong for the Future: Modernizing Our Union Constitution & Bylaws 

No matter what we look like, where we come from, or what job we do, working people deserve dignity, safety, and a voice on the job by organizing their union. But powerful interests try to divide us and weaken our ability to stand up for what we need. That’s why we’re taking action to ensure efficient use of our resources while strengthening and protecting our local Union — by updating SEIU Local 49’s Constitution and Bylaws. These updates will make our Union more modern, more inclusive, and more transparent — so we can keep fighting and winning together. 

A lot has changed in the last 15 years. Think about it: 15 years ago, there was no Zoom, most of us didn’t have smartphones, and many of our strongest union leaders today hadn’t even started their jobs yet. Just like our workplaces and organizing have evolved, it’s time for our union’s rules to catch up. We’re also updating outdated language to make sure everyone in our union is respected, no matter our race, gender, or where we were born, so that every member is recognized and respected for who they are.  

One important note with all these changes: The proposed amendments to the bylaws do not increase member dues; in fact, this ensures no one will pay initiation fees and dues at the same time! 

Our SEIU Local 49 Executive Board voted unanimously to approve these updates. Now we need to hear from you. This is your union — and your voice matters. That’s why we’re asking all members to vote on these changes.

We'll have a booth set up where you can cast your vote. There will be grilling, pop & water, live music,  and more! Bring a side dish to share. NOTE: No alcohol allowed.

# Unión Fuerte para el Futuro: Modernizando nuestra Constitución y Reglamentos de la unión

No importa cómo nos veamos, de dónde vengamos o qué trabajo hagamos, las personas trabajadoras merecen dignidad, seguridad y una voz en el trabajo al organizar su unión. Pero los intereses poderosos intentan dividirnos y debilitar nuestra capacidad de luchar por lo que necesitamos. title: Northridge Indivisible Speaker Series - REPARATIONS
description:
Join us for a powerful and timely conversation as Mandla Kayise—Commissioner at the Civil, Human Rights and Equity Department for the City of Los Angeles—speaks on reparations and presents the department’s groundbreaking report, An Examination of African-American Experiences in Los Angeles.

Mandla Kayise is the President and CEO of New World Education (NWE), a consulting organization dedicated to empowering education professionals and communities. For over two decades, he has worked across California’s education system and in local and national community development efforts, helping build pathways to success for students, professionals, and marginalized communities. Before founding NWE, he served as a director of Student Affairs and Retention at UCLA and as a project manager at the Community Coalition of South Los Angeles.

A longtime advocate for racial equity, Mandla has been recognized by organizations such as the Los Angeles NAACP Youth League, Black Women for Wellness, and the UCLA Bunche Center for African American Studies. He currently serves on several nonprofit and educational boards and is a member of the Los Angeles Reparations Advisory Commission.

Don't miss this opportunity to hear from a leader whose work continues to shape the future of equity and justice in Los Angeles.

description:
**In America, we don’t put up with would-be kings.**
NO KINGS is a national day of action and mass mobilization in response to increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption from Trump and his allies. We’ve watched as they’ve cracked down on free speech, detained people for their political views, threatened to deport American citizens, and defied the courts. They’ve done this all while continuing to serve and enrich their billionaire allies.


🚨**On Saturday, June 14, we’re taking to the streets nationwide. We’re not gathering to feed his ego. We’re building a movement that leaves him behind.**🚨


The flag doesn’t belong to Donald Trump. It belongs to us. We’re not watching history happen. We’re making it.


**On June 14th, we’re showing up everywhere he isn’t—to say no thrones, no crowns, no kings.**
Check out nokings.org for more information.

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*
